- **What first sparked your curiosity about how the human body actually works? For me, it started with injuries. Growing up, distance running was a big part of my life. I was team captain, all-state, the athlete that showed up early and stayed late. Like many young athletes, I believed effort solved everything. Run more miles. Train harder. Push through. Until my body stopped cooperating. By the end of high school, injuries like IT band pain and patellar tendonitis forced me to spend more time with physical therapists than on the track. What stayed with me wasn’t just the treatment. It was the questions. Why does the same training produce different outcomes for different people? Why do small imbalances turn into bigger problems? Why does recovery sometimes matter as much as effort? That curiosity led me toward kinesiology and an early plan to pursue sports medicine, driven by a simple motivation: helping people understand their bodies and achieve the health they’re capable of. My career ultimately took a different direction. But that curiosity about human health and performance never really left. It’s still part of what draws me to healthcare today.
